item.body:
### Summary
As a user changing the dark style on an iPhone, I want to stay on Réglages › Thème after my pick, so that I see the result and can change it again. Today a switch between Standard and Plus sombre / Noir OLED pops the Plus tab back to its root, collapses the tab bar, and resets the scroll of the other tabs' lists.

### Facts
- Mac check of #589 (2026-11-10, comment 6771230994), iPhone simulator iOS 27.0, build `fddb6a37`: 2 of 2 picks (Standard → Plus sombre, Noir OLED → Standard). Darker ↔ OLED does not pop. iPad keeps every column and the reader.
- LOT-122's spec announces it (« a change of style in Settings rebuilds the screens it wraps; transient state resets »): the Standard ↔ Darker/OLED switch changes the view structure (#589 option (b)).
- Related observation: on plain iPhone screens « Plus sombre » (`#0B0B0C`) is slightly lighter than Standard's system `#000000`.

### Decision needed (operator)
Accept (documented trade-off) or keep the Settings stack and list positions across the rebuild. Recommendation: keep the stack (navigation path held above the rebuilt subtree), since losing the screen where the choice was made reads as a bug.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a style pick, Réglages › Thème stays on screen and the other tabs keep their stack and scroll.
- [ ] A test proves the navigation path survives the style change.

Refs #589, LOT-122 (#213).
